source.notes: Wisconsin (275) on Jake confirmed by Stoopids Site on October 31, 2026; the input had no slot for it, so it sits at overall 63 (round 8, pick 7), the only open slot. Graded like any other pick.

Jim.summary4: Nasty Peacock tops the board with an A+, and Jim gets to strut a little. Arizona (power rank #6) and Michigan St (#11) came back-to-back at picks 7 and 10, a one-two punch nobody else matched. Three SEC schools (Vanderbilt, Kentucky, Texas A&M) give the middle real muscle. Indiana at pick 58 was a sneaky-good closer to cap it all off.
Jim.deep: Nasty Peacock finishes 1st of 8 with an A+. Its strength score is 65.9 out of 100, the best in the league. The league average is 54.5, so Nasty Peacock sits 11.4 points above it. Arizona (power rank #6, Big 12) is the anchor and projects as a 2 seed. Michigan St (#11) at pick 10 gave Jim two top-11 schools before most rosters had one. Vanderbilt at pick 23 with a power rank of #19 kept the early run going. Kentucky at pick 26 (rank #35) came a touch early, but a projected 7 seed is a fine round-4 piece. The roster spans 5 conferences, led by the SEC with 3 schools. North Carolina at #58 is the lowest-ranked school and the one to keep an eye on. Every school on this roster has a power rank, so there are no blank spots at all.

Paul.summary4: Party Paul lands a sharp A, 2nd of 8 and just 1.3 points behind the top spot. UConn (power rank #4) leads, with Iowa State (#13) and Nebraska (#16) right behind. All 8 schools are ranked, spread across 7 different conferences. Howard at pick 59 with a power rank of #28 might be the late-round grab of the whole draft.
Paul.deep: Party Paul finishes 2nd of 8 with an A. Its strength score is 64.6 out of 100, 10.1 points above the league average of 54.5. UConn (power rank #4, Big East) is the anchor and projects as a 2 to 3 seed. Iowa State (#13) at pick 11 and Nebraska (#16) at pick 22 make a sturdy second and third. McNeese at pick 27 with a power rank of #20 was another nice value. Howard at pick 59 came 31 spots after its power rank of #28, the biggest value on this roster. Wichita St (#27) at pick 43 was a quiet win too. The Big East has 2 schools, and no other conference has more than 1. Villanova at #39 is the lowest-ranked school, and that is a pretty high floor. Every school here has a power rank, so Party Paul is built to stay in the race all season.

Jake.summary4: Stock Rising grabs an A- and 3rd place, powered by the top-ranked school in the field, Duke. St John's, Texas and Saint Mary's give Jake a solid ranked core behind the Blue Devils. Wisconsin in round 8 gives Jake a second Big Ten school. Tennessee St at pick 50 was a bold call, and bold calls make March fun.
Jake.deep: Stock Rising finishes 3rd of 8 with an A-. Its strength score is 57.5 out of 100, 3 points above the league average of 54.5. Duke is the anchor, power rank #1 and a projected 1 seed. St John's (#17) at pick 15 and Texas (#15) at pick 18 came right around their rankings. Saint Mary's at pick 31 with a power rank of #23 was the best value on the roster. UCLA (#42) at pick 34 is a projected 8 seed. Auburn (#74) at pick 47 and Wisconsin (#77) at pick 63 add two more power-conference schools. Tennessee St at pick 50 (rank #79) was the earliest call relative to its rank. The roster spans 6 conferences, with the SEC and Big Ten tied at 2 each. Every school is ranked, so the depth question is about how high, not whether.

Kurt.summary4: Kurmoji earns a B+ for Kurt, 4th of 8 and just above the league average. Virginia (power rank #8) leads a front three with Louisville and Tennessee, all top-21 schools. The roster spreads evenly across the ACC, SEC and Big Ten with 2 apiece. It is a steady, sensible build that should hang around all season.
Kurt.deep: Kurmoji finishes 4th of 8 with a B+. Its strength score is 56.8 out of 100, 2.3 points above the league average of 54.5. Virginia (power rank #8, ACC) is the anchor and projects as a 4 seed. Louisville (#18) at pick 14 and Tennessee (#21) at pick 19 came right on schedule. USC at pick 35 with a power rank of #38 was close to its spot too. BYU at pick 30 (rank #41) came a little early. Missouri went at pick 46 with a power rank of #46, a perfect match. Nevada (#60) is projected as a 12 seed and could be a fun spoiler. The ACC, SEC and Big Ten have 2 schools each, with BYU and Nevada filling out 5 conferences. Iowa at pick 62 is the only unranked school, so Kurt's depth is in good shape.

Ken.summary4: Kentut gets a B for Ken, 5th of 8 and a hair above the league average. Illinois (power rank #5) leads, and High Point (#9) at pick 13 was a gutsy, high-upside call. NC State at pick 61 with a power rank of #40 was a lovely late find. Seven conferences on one roster means Ken has a rooting interest almost everywhere.
Ken.deep: Kentut finishes 5th of 8 with a B. Its strength score is 56.3 out of 100, 1.8 points above the league average of 54.5. Illinois (power rank #5, Big Ten) is the anchor and projects as a 2 seed. High Point (#9) at pick 13 is ranked high but projects as a 13 seed, a fun mix. Arkansas (#22) at pick 20 and VCU (#24) at pick 36 add solid middle depth. NC State at pick 61 came 21 spots after its power rank of #40, the best value on the roster. Georgia at pick 45 (rank #61) was the earliest call relative to its rank. The SEC leads with 2 schools in a 7-conference mix. Vermont (#64) is projected as a 16 seed and is the lowest-ranked school. Every school is ranked, so Kentut has no empty slots to worry about.

Mark.summary4: Dirty Draymond gets a B- for Mark, 6th of 8. Florida at pick 1 (power rank #2) is a strong place to start any roster. Texas Tech and Alabama, back-to-back at the turn, add two projected 5 seeds. Tulsa at pick 64 is unranked, so Mark is counting on Florida to carry the party.
Mark.deep: Dirty Draymond finishes 6th of 8 with a B-. Its strength score is 51.9 out of 100, 2.6 points below the league average of 54.5. Florida (power rank #2, SEC) is the anchor and projects as a 1 seed. Texas Tech (#25) at pick 16 and Alabama (#29) at pick 17 both project as 5 seeds. Utah State at pick 32 with a power rank of #30 came right on time. UC Irvine at pick 33 (rank #63) was the earliest call relative to its rank. Akron (#49) and Cincinnati (#50) went at picks 48 and 49, right around their ranks. The SEC and Big 12 tie with 2 schools each across 6 conferences. Tulsa at pick 64 is the only unranked school. A 1-seed anchor gives this roster a real shot to climb.

Scotty.summary4: En Fuego gets a C for Scotty, 7th of 8, but the top of this roster is spicy. Kansas (power rank #10) and Gonzaga (#3) at picks 8 and 9 are a fantastic turn. Miami at pick 25 with a power rank of #14 was a lovely value. Three unranked late picks (Boise St, Colgate, Princeton) are what pull the grade down.
Scotty.deep: En Fuego finishes 7th of 8 with a C. Its strength score is 47.4 out of 100, 7.1 points below the league average of 54.5. Gonzaga (power rank #3, Pac-12) is the anchor and projects as a 3 seed. Kansas (#10) at pick 8 is also a projected 3 seed, so the top two are strong. Miami at pick 25 came 11 spots after its power rank of #14, the best value on the roster. Purdue at pick 24 (rank #45) was the earliest call relative to its rank. Ohio State (#37) at pick 41 projects as an 8 seed. Boise St, Colgate and Princeton are unranked, and an unranked school scores 0 in the grade. The Pac-12 and Big Ten tie with 2 schools each across 6 conferences. If the top four deliver, En Fuego can still turn up the heat.

Murf.summary4: Murfcockchalkrock gets a D for Murf, 8th of 8, but it starts with a bang. Houston (power rank #7) and Michigan (#26) give Murf two projected top-6 seeds. Grand Canyon at pick 28 with a power rank of #12 was one of the best values in the whole draft. Three unranked schools (Memphis, Drake, Grambling) are what sink the grade, so there is plenty of room to rise.
Murf.deep: Murfcockchalkrock finishes 8th of 8 with a D. Its strength score is 35.7 out of 100, 18.8 points below the league average of 54.5. Houston (power rank #7, Big 12) is the anchor and projects as a 2 seed. Michigan (#26) at pick 12 projects as a 6 seed. Grand Canyon at pick 28 came 16 spots after its power rank of #12, the best value on the roster. San Diego St at pick 21 (rank #69) was the earliest call relative to its rank. Wright St (#70) projects as a 14 to 15 seed. Memphis, Drake and Grambling are unranked, and an unranked school scores 0 in the grade. All 8 schools come from 8 different conferences, the widest spread in the league. Murf has the most room to climb of anyone, and that makes for a fun season.
